title: binding the compiler-recognized Context.context member to its capability and calling the bound result is the same detachment, refused at the same rule
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Context Access': '`Capability.context()` MUST be an inherited, compiler-recognized call on subclasses of `Context`.' `Reader.context.bind(Reader)()` reads the capability with the correct receiver and reaches the recognizer as `Function.prototype.bind` applied to a value — there is no `Capability.context()` call node anywhere in the program. It is written as a SEPARATE case from `a-detached-context-reference-is-rejected` rather than folded into it, and the reason is measured rather than stylistic: on the pre-fix tree the two spellings had DIFFERENT verdicts on different backends. The `Reflect.apply` form was accepted by both; this `.bind` form was refused by the reference (incidentally, `TS2571`) and ACCEPTED by the fork, which is the backend-verdict divergence the round-6 review filed under its Finding 3. One case covering only the Reflect form would have left the divergent half unpinned, and one covering only the bind form would have missed the accepted-and-running half. Together they pin that the rule is about the detachment and not about the consumer, on both backends, at each program's own position. Column 10 on line 8 is `Reader.context`, the member selection — the same node the sibling case declares, reached through a different consumer. PIN THE SMITHERS CODE, NOT THE TYPESCRIPT ONE: the reference's old `TS2571` here was a typing accident, not a rule, and it is gone now that the frontend refuses first and short-circuits the emitted-TypeScript stage. Declaring it would ratify the accident and would break the moment either prelude's typing of `context` changed for an unrelated reason. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the message (SMITHERS2107's sentence carries no payload), and the `.call` / `.apply` / alias / destructuring / template-interpolation spellings, which both backends now refuse at the same code and position and which the implementations' own tests enumerate — the corpus carries the two that had different verdicts, not all seventeen. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared line from 8 to 9 turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 a0ee5041b8408218f1208bb5ae79fb9c16d85a6e25619473ba828c0b0bfcbb65 before and after).
